notes: Full current MLA rosters for Jammu & Kashmir (95: 90 elected + 5 LG-nominated, all 5 nominated seats VACANT as of 2026-09-25 per Sept 2026 news), Arunachal Pradesh (60), Manipur (60: 58 filled + 2 vacant due to MLA deaths - Tadubi and Thanlon), and Meghalaya (60). Sourced from Wikipedia 'Nth Assembly' member-list pages (wikitext via parse API, fetched in chunks due to page size / WebFetch summarization limits) cross-checked against by-election articles. Current (post-defection/post-bypoll) party is used throughout, not the original 2022-2024 election-night party. Party-wise strength counts for AR, MN, JK were independently re-derived here and cross-validated exactly against the pre-existing entity stats in data/raw/states-ar-mn-ml.json and data/raw/states-dl-jk-la.json (written by a sibling segment) - full agreement on every party's seat count for all four legislatures, which is strong corroboration. AITC used (not the sibling file's 'MAITC') per this segment's standard-abbreviation instructions for Meghalaya's Trinamool Congress state unit. KNOWN GAPS (declared, not guessed): (1) J&K MLA wikipedia URLs are constructed from the member's plain name (name.replace(' ','_')) rather than verified individual wikilink targets, because the WebFetch chunks used for JK returned de-wikified plain text; some may 404 or land on a disambiguation page. AR/MN/ML wikipedia URLs are closer to the actual wikilink targets since those chunks retained wikitext. (2) The exact single Meghalaya constituency whose poll was deferred to 10 May 2023 (vs 27 Feb 2023) was not identified. (3) Gambegre (Meghalaya) by-election date given as 2024-11-23 from general knowledge of the November 2024 Indian by-election batch, not independently confirmed with a fetched source - flagged medium confidence on that one date only. (4) WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this segment ran; all research here was done via WebFetch + curl/python against Wikipedia (curl/python were rate-limited 429 throughout by a shared egress IP, consistent with sibling segments' notes, so WebFetch was the only working path).

stats.note: 90 elected seats + 5 LG-nominated seats provided for by the 2023 amendment to the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019; all 5 nominated seats remain VACANT as of 2026-09-25 (LG has not made nominations; ongoing political dispute over voting rights of nominated members).

Continued to exist through the 2025-26 President's Rule period (13 Feb 2025 - 4 Feb 2026); government reformed 4 Feb 2026 under CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh (BJP-NPP-NPF-JD(U) coalition). Tadubi and Thanlon seats vacant following MLA deaths.
One seat's poll was deferred to 10 May 2023 (exact seat not confirmed by this segment - declared gap). Meghalaya's council of ministers was reshuffled/expanded 16 Sept 2025.
